title: Strict finite germ comparisons on whole coefficient systems
statement: Fix a prime ell, a finite extension E of Q_ell, and a finite-field datum D. There exists strict data T of [def-trf-stalk-compositor-tower-data] satisfying TrfStrictStalkTowerCoherent: finitePullback preserves inverse-image unit generators; c is the published finite pullback-stalk germ map in each degree and exponent; gamma inserts the identity pointed neighbourhood; e is gamma followed by c at the identity point; the finite section, composition, identity and automorphism-reparametrization equations hold on the entire actual coefficient towers.

source.place: Tag 0F4F (lemma-point-functor): the combined-colimit identification behind the finite composition germ formula; agent extension to the entire-tower counit realization, original Steps 3, 6, 7; blueprint thm-trf-l-function-euler-product.proof.md, Step 1, Local powers, input (b).

proof.text: Take the mate of the sectionwise direct-image evaluation square, then identify the finite inverse image with the constant-ring inverse image by uniqueness of left adjoints preserving units. This constructs finitePullback and proves finiteUnit.

Apply the canonical finite germ comparison degreewise. The completed scalar acts through the same quotient on both sides. A differential or quotient transition merely replaces the section in the germ, so the maps and their inverses assemble to natural maps of whole towers.

Identity-point sections compute the stalk using the initial identity neighbourhood. Define e as gamma after pullback followed by c. Specialize finite composition to (v,id) for finiteSections, and use general composition and identity for the remaining equations.

Reindex lifts by Spec(alpha), leaving neighbourhood and section unchanged. Reindexing by its inverse gives the inverse. Both routes in the strict square produce the lift pr_V theta u Spec(alpha); transitions and differentials preserve this computation.

proof_origin.place: Stacks Tags 0F4F, 05V1 and 0941; strict-diagram and localization argument for Local powers (b).
